audience_description: Classroom teachers in Eduversal partner schools delivering the Cambridge curriculum (Lower Secondary, IGCSE, AS/A Level) alongside the national curriculum. Teachers report through the school's approved academic structure, normally through the Head of Department / Subject Leader and the Academic Coordinator / Principal (Career Growth: Framework 26-27 §10.1). Teachers in their Teacher Induction period (3 semesters) get the induction overlay tasks and are not on the F2 appraisal schedule.

regulatory_anchors.relevance: Defines teacher duty under principal supervision including planning, instruction, and assessment.

regulatory_anchors.title: Permendikdasmen 13/2025 — Pendekatan Pembelajaran Mendalam
regulatory_anchors.relevance: Deep learning approach, 8 dimensi profil lulusan.

regulatory_anchors.relevance: Standar Isi, Standar Proses, Standar Penilaian apply to teacher practice.

regulatory_anchors.relevance: Cambridge subject delivery standards and syllabus compliance.

framework_anchors.cambridge_teacher_standards_2023: Used for task mapping; tasks tagged with CTS reference where applicable.
framework_anchors.teacher_appraisal_handbook_26_27: Tasks build evidence for F1 Administration, F2 Class Observation (formal observations by the school's appraisers only), F3 Work Inspection (evidence presented at the End-of-Year Conference) and F4 Student Survey. Primary & Secondary weights 20 / 50 / 20 / 10; Early Years 20 / 60 / 20 (F4 not administered).

priority_levels.compliance: Legally required by Indonesian regulation OR contractually required by Cambridge/Eduversal. Non-negotiable.
priority_levels.core: Essential to effective performance. Strongly expected.
priority_levels.recommended: Best practice. Adopt where school context allows.

recurring_tasks.title: Submit lesson plans for the coming week
recurring_tasks.description: Submit your lesson plans by the school's deadline, using the Teaching & Learning: Lesson Planning Guide & Template 26-27. The minimum components include the curriculum reference, learning objective(s), success criteria, prior learning, the teaching and learning sequence with timing, differentiation and learner support, resources, checks for understanding, closure, and your reflection and next steps.
evidence_required: Lesson plans submitted in the school system
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: The template is a minimum structure, not a script or a paperwork exercise. A learning objective says what students will learn, not what they will do: 'Students will be able to solve simultaneous linear equations using elimination and explain why the method works', not 'Teach simultaneous equations'.
recurring_tasks.missed_threshold_action: Lesson plan submission timeliness is item F1.3 of your appraisal.

recurring_tasks.title: Add a short reflection after each lesson
recurring_tasks.description: Record a short professional reflection and next step in the lesson plan — what worked, and what you will change next time based on what students showed you.
evidence_required: Reflection recorded in the lesson plan
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: Don't write 'lesson went well'. Write what you saw: 'Students struggled with the second example because they didn't have the key vocabulary — next time pre-teach the four key terms in the starter.'

recurring_tasks.title: Try your agreed growth-focus strategy
recurring_tasks.description: If you and your Subject Leader agreed a growth focus this semester, use the chosen strategy in your lessons this week and notice the evidence you agreed to look for. At the next check-in, reflect first, then decide together: keep, adapt or replace.
recurring_tasks.applies_when: teacher has an agreed capacity-building focus (not a teacher in Teacher Induction)
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: One focus, at most two per semester. Capacity building is developmental and separate from appraisal.

recurring_tasks.title: Return marked work with specific feedback
recurring_tasks.description: Return marked work with specific, timely feedback that tells each student what to do next, following the Assessment Policy and your department's marking practice.
evidence_required: Marked work returned with next-step feedback
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: A grade alone is not feedback. Feedback tells the student what to do next: 'Your conclusion needs to reference Source B — rewrite the final paragraph.'

recurring_tasks.title: Check for understanding in every lesson
recurring_tasks.description: Plan checks for understanding — mini-whiteboards, exit tickets, cold-calling, hinge questions — and adjust the lesson based on what students show.
evidence_required: Checks for understanding named in the lesson plan
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: 'Thumbs up if you understand' is not a check for understanding. Use a technique that produces evidence — 'Show me on your whiteboard the answer to Q3' — then act on what you see.

recurring_tasks.title: Teacher-Paced Test this week (if scheduled)
recurring_tasks.description: If the Annual Plan in Edunav places a Teacher-Paced Test (EASE Assessment / Common Assessment) for your class this week, deliver it during the class's regular period — online through Latihan.id or on paper — and enter the results in Edunav.
recurring_tasks.applies_when: a Teacher-Paced Test is scheduled for your class in the Annual Plan

recurring_tasks.title: Keep your F3 evidence as you go
recurring_tasks.description: File this week's evidence of professional work — professional learning and what changed in your practice, collaboration, communication with families. F3 Work Inspection evidence is gathered through the year and presented by you at the End-of-Year Conference.
evidence_required: Evidence filed with a short impact note
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: Build it as you go — don't assemble it the night before the conference.

recurring_tasks.title: Complete attendance and grade entries on time
recurring_tasks.description: Record attendance every day. Enter every summative assessment score in the Edunav Gradebook within five working days.
recurring_tasks.specific_timing: Daily for attendance; within five working days for summative scores
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: Late attendance is a student-safety risk (parents are not told about an absence). Late grade entry breaks the report-card pipeline.

recurring_tasks.title: Read walkthrough feedback when you receive it
recurring_tasks.description: School leaders and Subject Leaders make short walkthroughs at any time, and the Principal walks through every classroom weekly. Written walkthrough feedback reaches you through Edunav. Read it and think about the question it asks. Walkthroughs are developmental: they carry no score and are not part of your F2 result.

recurring_tasks.title: Formal observation this week (if scheduled)
recurring_tasks.description: The school's appraisers — Subject Leader / Head of Department, Principal, Academic or Cambridge Coordinator — formally observe you at least three times per semester. Before a formal observation, make sure your lesson plan is submitted and read the Pre-Observation Information. Afterwards, join the post-observation conference (Glow / Grow / Go) and agree your next step. These formal observations, recorded in Edunav Appraisal, are the only source of your F2 score; Eduversal Subject Specialist visits are formative only.
recurring_tasks.applies_when: a formal observation is scheduled; teachers in the Teacher Appraisal population (not in Teacher Induction)
framework_anchor: Teacher Appraisal: Handbook 26-27 — F2 Class Observation

fortnightly_tasks.title: Department meeting
fortnightly_tasks.description: Your department meets at least every two weeks. Come with the actions you own, student work or data when it is on the agenda, and any resource, safety or access problem. Leave with named actions, owners and due dates.
evidence_required: Your actions recorded in the department action tracker
framework_anchor: Department Handbook Template 26-27 — Department meeting rhythm
fortnightly_tasks.first_time_guide: Department meetings are developmental: shared planning, resources, moderation and short professional learning. They never produce an appraisal score or a teacher ranking.

termly_tasks.title: End-of-semester reflection and Student Survey
termly_tasks.description: At the end of each semester, students complete the Student Survey through their own Edunav accounts (F4 — Primary and Secondary only). Read your own progress on your growth focus before the progress conversation with your Subject Leader.

termly_tasks.title: EASE Academic this semester (if your subject takes part)
termly_tasks.description: EASE Academic is a teacher exam, once per semester, for teachers of English, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Integrated Science: 50 multiple-choice questions in 120 minutes on Latihan.id. Check your date on the EASE Academic tab of the EASE Schedule 26-27 and prepare with the four free GPK resources. It is formative only: your individual score is shared with you alone and never feeds your appraisal.
termly_tasks.applies_when: you teach English, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology or Integrated Science

1.phase: August — Tahun ajaran baru begins; MPLS
1.focus: Establishing routines, learning student names, baseline diagnostic prep

tasks.title: Establish your classroom routines before instruction begins
tasks.description: Define and rehearse your routines — how students enter, how they move between tasks, how you get full attention — following Teaching & Learning: Learning Environment 26-27.
framework_anchor: Teacher Appraisal F2 — Classroom Management domain
tasks.first_time_guide: Routines are the precondition for everything else. A teacher with weak routines cannot deliver effective instruction in November either. Spend the time now.

tasks.title: Learn the names of every student in every class you teach
tasks.description: By the end of Week 1, you should be able to greet every student by name without prompting.
tasks.first_time_guide: This is a relationship investment that pays back every day for the rest of the year. Use a seating plan with photos.

tasks.title: Read the Academic Integrity and AI Responsible Use policies
tasks.description: Read Digital Citizenship & AI Appendix A (Academic Integrity Policy 26-27) and Appendix B (AI Responsible Use Policy 26-27), and tell your classes where the boundaries are before the first piece of work is handed in.
evidence_required: Policies read and communicated to classes
framework_anchor: Digital Citizenship & AI Framework — Appendices A and B
tasks.first_time_guide: Most AI-honesty disputes happen when the boundary was never stated at the start of the year.

2.focus: Diagnostic assessment to establish starting points for each class

tasks.title: Run a baseline diagnostic for each class you teach
tasks.description: A short, low-stakes diagnostic that shows each student's starting point in your subject. It is not a graded test — use it to plan differentiation.
tasks.first_time_guide: Your scheme of work assumes prior learning. Do not assume — check. The baseline tells you who needs scaffolding and who needs extension.

tasks.title: Check your students' Cambridge entries (if you teach IGCSE / AS / A Level)
tasks.description: Help with subject and tier decisions when you are asked, and check with the Exams Officer that your October/November candidates appear on the confirmed entries for the right syllabus, tier and components. Standard October/November entries close before September.
tasks.applies_when: subject is IGCSE / AS / A-Level Cambridge
evidence_required: Entries checked with the Exams Officer
tasks.first_time_guide: Wrong entries mean a student sits the wrong paper. Double-check the syllabus code, the option and the tier.

tasks.title: Run final exam preparation for Cambridge candidates
tasks.description: If you teach a Cambridge subject with October/November candidates: final review using past papers, mark schemes and command-word practice. The series runs from late September to mid-November.
tasks.applies_when: subject is IGCSE / AS / A-Level Cambridge with Oct/Nov candidates
tasks.first_time_guide: Show students how examiners read command words — 'describe', 'explain' and 'evaluate' earn marks differently.

tasks.title: EASE Week 1 — EASE Growth, lessons continue
tasks.description: EASE Growth runs this week for Grades 7-12, normally in the first two periods on the grade band's day (Wednesday Grades 7-8, Thursday Grades 9-10, Friday Grades 11-12). Normal lessons continue. EASE Growth is never graded and is not entered in the Gradebook; in 2026-27 it is a baseline.

14.week_label: EASE Week 2 — Semester I Synchronized Test

tasks.title: Prepare your students for the Synchronized Test
tasks.description: Familiarise students with the online format on Latihan.id and the timing. The Synchronized Test is taken on the same day and time across the network. During the official window students see only their score; questions open for review after the window closes.
tasks.first_time_guide: Common Assessment replaces the old Quiz / Mid-Term / Final categories for Grades 7-12. Approved school-level Assessment evidence may inform the School Appraisal; it never scores you as an individual.

tasks.title: Run the Synchronized Test and enter the results
tasks.description: EASE Week 2: normal lessons stop for the network testing block. Supervise as scheduled, mark any manually graded questions with the M1 / A1 / B1 mark scheme, and enter the results in Edunav. Where the live EASE Schedule replaces the test with a Cambridge exam for your grade and subject, follow the schedule.

16.focus: Moderation of Semester I summative marking

tasks.title: Take part in department moderation
tasks.description: Review a sample of student work with colleagues and resolve marking differences against the agreed criteria and rubrics.
tasks.first_time_guide: If your marking differs from a colleague's on the same script, that is the conversation worth having. Don't defend your mark — look at the criteria together.

tasks.title: Write Semester I report comments for every student
tasks.description: Each comment should name specific evidence of progress and a clear next step. Avoid generic 'good progress' comments.
tasks.first_time_guide: Parents read the comment, not only the grade. A specific next step is worth more than 'great work, keep it up'.

tasks.title: Archive Semester I lesson materials and work samples
tasks.description: Organise lesson plans, marked work samples and reflections for next year's planning and your F3 evidence.

19.focus: Reset routines, agree Semester II focus

tasks.title: Reset classroom routines and re-state expectations
tasks.description: After the break, re-ground students in your classroom routines. Treat the first lesson back like Week 1.

tasks.title: Agree your Semester II growth focus with your Subject Leader
tasks.description: If your focus now reads 'Now Consistent', agree the second priority; otherwise continue the same focus into Semester II.
tasks.applies_when: teacher has an agreed capacity-building focus

tasks.title: EASE Week 3 — EASE Growth, lessons continue
tasks.description: EASE Growth runs again for Grades 7-12 (exam-heavy grades may sit earlier). Normal lessons continue; it is not graded and not entered in the Gradebook.

tasks.title: Check your May/June Cambridge entries
tasks.description: Check with the Exams Officer that your May/June candidates are entered for the correct syllabus, options and tiers.
tasks.applies_when: subject is IGCSE / AS / A-Level Cambridge
evidence_required: Entries checked with the Exams Officer

tasks.title: Exam-period teaching priorities
tasks.description: The Cambridge May/June series is running. Final review for candidates; for classes without candidates, keep the normal teaching rhythm.

33.week_label: EASE Week 4 — Semester II Synchronized Test

tasks.title: Run the Semester II Synchronized Test and enter the results
tasks.description: EASE Week 4: normal lessons stop. Same routine as EASE Week 2 — online through Latihan.id, M1 / A1 / B1 marking for manually graded questions, results in Edunav, and the live EASE Schedule decides where a Cambridge exam replaces the test.

tasks.title: Finish Semester II marking and Gradebook entries
tasks.description: Complete the semester's marking and enter every summative score in the Edunav Gradebook within five working days, ready for moderation and reports.

tasks.title: Prepare your F3 evidence for the End-of-Year Conference
tasks.description: Organise the evidence of your professional work from the year — professional learning and its impact, collaboration, communication with families — so you can present it at the End-of-Year Conference.
tasks.first_time_guide: A well-organised evidence set turns the conference into a professional conversation rather than a judgement event.

tasks.title: Attend your End-of-Year Conference
tasks.description: You present your F3 evidence; your appraiser scores F3 only after that. The annual F2 is the mean of your valid formal observations, and F4 is the mean of the Semester 1 and Semester 2 Student Survey results. The composite is calculated only when every applicable framework is complete. You agree next year's objectives, and the final record reaches you through Edunav.
tasks.applies_when: teacher in the Teacher Appraisal population (not in Teacher Induction)
framework_anchor: Teacher Appraisal: Handbook 26-27 — Full Appraisal Cycle
tasks.first_time_guide: Read your record carefully in Edunav and use it to draft your personal professional goal for next year.

tasks.title: Archive year materials and prepare handover notes
tasks.description: Organise the full year's lesson materials. If a class is moving to a different teacher next year, prepare handover notes (cohort strengths, ongoing concerns, students who need continued support).

extra_tasks_first_12_weeks.title: Mentor session
extra_tasks_first_12_weeks.description: Meet your mentor: 15 minutes daily in Weeks 1-3 (Familiarization), then a weekly 1-hour session for the rest of Semester 1 (Foundation). Bring a specific question or concern.

extra_tasks_first_12_weeks.title: Monthly mentor observation
extra_tasks_first_12_weeks.description: Your mentor observes one lesson a month from Month 2 to Month 9 (30-45 minutes) and holds a 10-15 minute debrief the same day. It is developmental and never feeds appraisal.
framework_anchor: Induction Module: Teacher 26-27 — The Observation Spine

extra_tasks_first_12_weeks.title: Induction journal entry
extra_tasks_first_12_weeks.description: A short reflection in your induction journal. By default only you and your mentor can see it; you may share an entry with your school leader when you want support.

extra_tasks_first_12_weeks.title: Weekly pulse (Friday)
extra_tasks_first_12_weeks.description: Answer one question — 'How was your week?' — on the 5-emoji scale. Your mentor and the authorised school induction lead see your answer so they can support you. Two low weeks in a row prompt a support follow-up; the pulse is never used for appraisal.

feeds_into: Teacher Appraisal F1-F4 evidence (official record in Edunav)
